question: For genes the compiled programs drive through two or more elements, does a reader-gated run under the multiplicative composition (Zhou et al. 2024: A = exp(G*W), basal 0, no parameter of its own) track measured RNA across the thirteen reader cell types better than a no-rule baseline, as 7d asked of the runtime's mean and the promoter-competition form; and on the genes all three forms run, is it closer to measured RNA than either of them?
census_sentence: of the 17,983 multi-element genes combine2.classify admits, the multiplicative composition makes 16,784 runnable (1,199 are not: 1199 inhibitor_strength_above_1) and 16,678 informative across the thirteen reader cells; 7d's forms made 4,779 (the runtime's mean) and 2,536 (promoter competition) informative, and 11,802 of the multiplicative form's informative genes are informative under neither 7d form (under the runtime's mean: 11396 basal_not_positive, 331 inhibitor_strength_above_1, 75 runnable_not_informative); 2,439 genes are informative under all three forms, before the RNA tables' row check
money: none: no request is sent and no key is read
reading: the multiplicative composition (Zhou et al. 2024): worse; the reader-gated run of genes with two or more compiled elements raised the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types above the no-rule baseline's (Delta MSE -0.5361 [97.5% CI -0.5637, -0.5088] over 214,617 gene-cell pairs, 16,509 genes; control p = 1). Head-to-head over the 2,405 genes in all three populations (31,265 gene-cell pairs), the multiplicative composition was closer to measured RNA than the runtime's mean (MSE(mean) - MSE(multiplicative) +0.04395 [97.5% CI +0.0385, +0.04979]) and closer to measured RNA than the promoter-competition form (Bothma 2015, declared half-occupied promoter) (MSE(competition) - MSE(multiplicative) +0.7383 [97.5% CI +0.6625, +0.8183]).

multiplicative.reading: the multiplicative composition (Zhou et al. 2024): worse; the reader-gated run of genes with two or more compiled elements raised the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types above the no-rule baseline's (Delta MSE -0.5361 [97.5% CI -0.5637, -0.5088] over 214,617 gene-cell pairs, 16,509 genes; control p = 1)

mean.clause: closer to measured RNA than the runtime's mean

competition.clause: closer to measured RNA than the promoter-competition form (Bothma 2015, declared half-occupied promoter)

limitations: independence: each element's removal fold comes from AlphaGenome's RNA-seq gene scorer (an in-silico deletion, the argmax over 371 RNA-seq tracks), a model trained on ENCODE and GTEx RNA-seq, with RNA-seq tracks named for the reader biosamples among them, and on ENCODE DNase-seq; the reader's open/closed calls are ENCODE DNase-seq narrowPeak files of the same biosamples; the measured outcome is ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of those biosamples, data of the kind, and possibly the very experiments, the model was trained on. The cross-cell pattern of a gated prediction comes from the DNase calls alone and the size of each element's part from the model

the fit treats a gene's k observations as taken at one intact state, but each is the argmax over 371 tracks in its own track, and each reader cell's run transports them there. A maximum per element inflates each element's fold, and under the multiplicative form every held element's fold enters the prediction in full, so the inflation widens the predicted range

the population is the genes the multiplicative fit runs, a different and larger set than either of 7d's (the census): the comparison against the baseline is not on 7d's genes, and only the head-to-heads are. The head-to-heads are on the genes all three forms run, those whose summed activating drops leave a positive basal rate under both of 7d's fits; nothing in them says how 7d's forms would read on the genes only the multiplicative form runs

the multiplicative form is Zhou et al. 2024's reading of enhancers perturbed together in one K562 CRISPRi screen (Gasperini 2019); here it composes every compiled element of a gene, up to dozens, in thirteen cell types, which that evidence does not cover. It sets the basal rate to 0: a gene's level with every element held is T*exp(-sum beta)/R0, and no level in molecules per cell is quoted

declared, not measured: the DECLARED_STRENGTH convention and the bridge's Hill assumptions (K = 1, n = 2, h = 0.5), which under this form decide only which inhibitors are feasible (RHO_j <= 2); no fold prediction depends on them

accessibility near a gene tracks its expression across cell types whatever any compiled rule says; an open element is one a rule may act through, not evidence that it does, and no reading here is evidence of a mechanism

one polyA plus experiment per biosample, from several labs; two of the thirteen are tissues (ovary, testis). Every rate under the run is mouse NIH 3T3 or their genome median; no fold prediction depends on it and no level in molecules per cell is quoted
7d's two forms are read here only through the head-to-heads; their own readings against the baseline are 7d's registered readings, quoted verbatim and not re-decided

context_verbatim.seven_d_reading: the runtime's mean: worse; the reader-gated run of genes with two or more compiled elements raised the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types above the no-rule baseline's (Delta MSE -0.4435 [97.5% CI -0.4843, -0.4085] over 61,425 gene-cell pairs, 4,725 genes; control p = 0.3); the promoter-competition form (Bothma 2015, declared half-occupied promoter): worse; the reader-gated run of genes with two or more compiled elements raised the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types above the no-rule baseline's (Delta MSE -0.8102 [97.5% CI -0.8994, -0.7252] over 32,513 gene-cell pairs, 2,501 genes; control p = 0.734). Head-to-head over the 2,405 genes in both populations, the promoter-competition form was further from measured RNA than the mean (MSE(mean) - MSE(competition) -0.6944 [95% CI -0.7613, -0.6288]).
context_verbatim.m2e_census_sentence: under the multiplicative composition 199 of the 210 genes the traced pairs reach are identifiable (11 are not: 11 inhibitor_strength_above_1); M2d ran 10 of them under the runtime's mean and 2 under promoter competition, and a concave composition with a positive basal rate, whatever its parameters, could fit at most the 12 whose activating single-removal drops sum to less than 1

result_manifest.assembly: GRCh38; RNA genes matched by gene_id through data/cache/gencode_genes.tsv

bootstrap.unit: gene: genes are resampled with replacement and carry all thirteen of their pairs
bootstrap.interval: the multiplicative form's 97.5% percentile interval, 7d's per-form interval (Bonferroni over 7d's two forms), kept so that the three forms' readings stand on one interval; each of the two head-to-heads 97.5% (Bonferroni over the two; 7d's one head-to-head was at 95%)

exclusions: genes with one rule, rules in several programs, or a measured rule
observations unreadable or exactly 1; no activating rule
multiplicative: an inhibitor with RHO > 2 or summed log-folds beyond EXPONENT_LIMIT; a prediction the same in all thirteen cells
genes whose symbol is not one gene_id, or whose gene_id is not on one row of every table
result_manifest.partitions: n/a: every qualifying gene is scored

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 5c620d3

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
